title: Company-wide policies and process: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the single source of truth for employees and managers to determine required approvals, ownership, and step-by-step procedures for routine and exceptional workflows.

Audience:
All Redwood employees; managers should ensure their teams follow the processes below. Security, Finance, People Ops, and IT own specific sections as indicated.

Table of contents:
1) Access & permissions
2) Change management
3) Data management
4) Procurement & expenses
5) Vendor management
6) Travel policies
7) Internal templates & examples
8) Contacts and escalation

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Access & permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access is enforced across systems, with a clear request/approval and periodic review process.
Owner: Security (RBAC) & IT (provisioning)
Policy highlights:
- Principle: Least privilege by default. Access is granted for a defined business purpose and duration.
- Classification: Accounts and resources are classified as: public, internal, restricted, and confidential. Higher classifications require stronger controls (MFA, SSO, approvals).
- Authentication: All accounts must use SSO (Okta) and MFA. Exceptions require documented compensation controls and Security approval.

Access request workflow (standard):
1. Requestor opens an Access Request ticket in the IT Service Portal (link: /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/access-requests).
2. Provide: resource name, required role (read/write/admin), business justification, and expiration date.
3. Manager approval (auto-cc: manager).
4. Owner team approval (Security or designated resource owner).
5. IT provisions access and adds ticket resolution notes.

Emergency access (e.g., incident triage):
1. Engineer requests emergency access via Slack #it-urgent + create ticket within 24 hours.
2. Pager duty on-call (Security or SRE) must approve within 1 hour.
3. Access is time-limited (max 4 hours) and audited.

Periodic review and deprovisioning:
- Quarterly access reviews are run by the Security team. Resource owners must certify users.
- On termination or role change, managers must submit a deprovisioning request within 24 hours to IT.

Approval table:
| Resource class | Approver (first) | Secondary approver | Max default duration | Notes |
|---------------|------------------|---------------------|----------------------|-------|
| Internal apps (read) | Manager | App owner | 90 days | Auto-expire unless renewed |
| Internal apps (write) | Manager | App owner & Security | 30 days | More frequent review |
| Production infra (admin) | Director | SRE Lead & Security | 7 days | Short-lived; require just-in-time |
| Confidential data | Director | CISO | 14 days | Requires training ack |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2) Change management
Purpose: Reduce risk to production systems by standardizing how changes are proposed, reviewed, and deployed.
Owner: Eng Platform & Eng SRE
Change categories:
- Standard change: Low risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine config updates).
- Normal change: Requires approval and CAB review for non-emergency modifications.
- Emergency change: Unplanned change to remediate a live incident.

Process for normal changes:
1. Create a Change Request (CR) in the Change Management system (link: /confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/change-requests). Include scope, rollback plan, test plan, expected impact, and timing.
2. Peer review by engineering owner.
3. Submit to Change Advisory Board (CAB) for approval if the expected impact > 5% of customers or is production-facing. CAB meets daily with asynchronous review windows.
4. After CAB approval, schedule change in maintenance window or low-impact slot.
5. Execute, document results, and update CR with post-deployment verification.

Emergency change procedure:
1. Declare emergency in the incident bridge.
2. On-call SRE + service owner approve immediate change.
3. Implement change with minimum blast radius; always include a rollback.
4. Post-incident: convert to CR and present to CAB within 3 business days for retrospective and permanent remediation plan.

Change testing and rollout guidance:
- Canary first: deploy to 5-10% of capacity and run synthetic checks for 30 minutes.
- Metrics to monitor: error-rate, p50/p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queue length. Abort if error-rate increases > 2x baseline or latency increases > 30% for p95.

Approval matrix (examples):
- Feature flag flip (non-prod): Standard change, no CAB.
- Database schema migration (prod): Normal change, CAB approval required, require rollback SQL and downtime plan.
- Runtime kernel upgrade on serving fleet: Normal/High-risk change, require risk assessment and SRE runbook.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3) Data management
Purpose: Protect customer and company data, ensure correct classification, retention, and handling.
Owner: Security & Data Privacy
Data classification and handling:
- Public: Non-sensitive material. Can be published.
- Internal: Company-internal documents and telemetry. Store in company drives with internal ACLs.
- Restricted: Customer data, credentials, internal models. Access only by approved roles.
- Confidential: PII/regulated data. Must be encrypted at rest, in transit; strict logging and approval for access.

Minimum controls by classification:
- Encryption: At rest and in transit for Restricted and Confidential.
- Logging: Access to Restricted/Confidential must be logged and retained for 1 year.
- Backups: Daily encrypted backups for critical datasets; retention policy specified below.

Retention policy (examples):
| Data type | Retention | Owner | Notes |
|----------|-----------|-------|-------|
| Audit logs | 1 year | Security | Immutable storage; legal hold process applies |
| Telemetry (aggregated) | 2 years | Eng Platform | Aggregated metrics can be retained longer if anonymized |
| Customer raw data | Customer-determined | Customer Success | Default: 90 days unless customer agreement stipulates otherwise |
| Payroll records | 7 years | Finance | Compliance requirement |

Data access review:
- Quarterly access reviews for systems storing Restricted/Confidential data.
- Data owners must maintain a data inventory (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).

Data breach response:
1. Follow Incident Response policy (see /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security).
2. Notify Legal and People Ops within 2 hours of confirmed breach.
3. Customer notification as required by contracts and law; coordinate with Legal.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4) Procurement & expenses
Purpose: Standardize procurement for software, hardware, and services; enforce budget controls and timely expense reimbursement.
Owner: Finance & Procurement
Procurement thresholds and approval flows:
- Low value (<= $5,000): Manager approval.
- Mid value ($5,001- $50,000): Director + Finance approval.
- High value (>$50,000): VP Finance + Legal + Executive sponsor.

Procurement steps (software/hardware/service):
1. Fill Procurement Request Form (template link: /confluence/policies-and-process/procurement-request-template). Include justification, vendor, estimated TCO, budget code.
2. Manager approval and budget check.
3. Finance approval (compliance and vendor screening).
4. Legal reviews contract terms for mid/high value or if data residency is involved.
5. Purchase order issued and procurement records stored in Procurement system.

Expenses and reimbursement:
- Employees submit expenses within 30 days using the Expense system with receipts attached.
- Travel expenses require pre-approval for international travel (>72 hours).
- Standard per diem and lodging caps are published in the Travel section below.

Emergency purchases:
- For incident-related purchases (e.g., burst capacity), Engineering Lead + Finance must approve; Finance will retroactively record as emergency procurement and archive justification.

Approved vendors and preferred discounts:
- Finance maintains a preferred vendors list with negotiated discounts. Always check preferred vendors before initiating a new vendor relationship.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5) Vendor management
Purpose: Ensure vendors meet security, privacy, and contractual standards; centralize onboarding and offboarding of third-party vendors.
Owner: Finance & Legal (vendor vetting) + Security (risk review)
Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Complete Vendor Request Form with business case and data access requirements.
2. Finance verifies procurement and budget.
3. Security performs a risk assessment (questionnaire + SOC2 or equivalent evidence for vendors handling sensitive data).
4. Legal reviews and signs contract (NDA, DPA, security addendum as needed).
5. Vendor account owner assigned and onboarding schedule agreed.

Vendor review cadence:
- Strategic vendors: quarterly business reviews.
- Standard vendors: annual security and performance review.
- Offboarding: revoke all vendor access within 24 hours of contract termination and confirm data disposal per contract.

Vendor risk categories and controls:
- Low risk: SaaS tools that do not handle customer data. Standard contract and periodic review.
- Medium risk: Tools that access internal systems or aggregated telemetry. Require SOC2 type II and IP protections.
- High risk: Vendors that store/process customer PII or model weights. Require encryption, data residency controls, and formal DPA.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6) Travel policies
Purpose: Keep employees safe while traveling and control travel spend.
Owner: People Ops & Finance
Pre-approval and booking:
- Domestic travel < 72 hours: Manager pre-approval via Travel Request form.
- International travel or travel > 72 hours: Director pre-approval and People Ops notification.
- Use preferred travel vendor/portal to book flights and hotels (preferred vendor list maintained by Finance).

Expense caps and guidelines:
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours; Business class allowed for flights > 6 hours with Director approval.
- Hotels: cap by city category (e.g., Tier 1 cities $250/night, Tier 2 $180/night). See detailed table in Travel Request template.
- Meals: per diem rates by country; retain receipts for all meals.

Safety & security:
- Register travel plans with People Ops for international travel.
- For high-risk locations, Security must review and provide travel guidance.

Travel emergency procedure:
1. If an employee is in immediate danger, contact local emergency services and notify People Ops and Security.
2. People Ops coordinates evacuation or temporary relocation if required.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7) Internal templates & examples
Purpose: Provide ready-to-use templates to standardize requests and reduce process friction. All templates live in the Templates library (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates). Examples included below.

Templates (quick list):
- Procurement Request Template (/confluence/policies-and-process/procurement-request-template)
- Access Request Template (/confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/access-request-template)
- Change Request Template (/confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/change-request-template)
- Vendor Risk Assessment (/confluence/finance-and-legal/vendor-risk-assessment)
- Travel Request Template (/confluence/policies-and-process/travel-request-template)

Example: Procurement Request Template (fields)
- Requestor name
- Manager
- Department
- Vendor name
- Spend estimate
- Budget code
- Business justification (200-400 words)
- Data access required (yes/no)
- Preferred contract term

Example: Change Request Template (fields)
- Title
- Owner and reviewers
- Scope and systems impacted
- Risk assessment and blast radius
- Rollback plan and test plan
- Monitoring checks and success criteria
- Scheduled window and approvers

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8) Contacts and escalation
Primary contacts:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Finance & Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Security & RBAC: security-ops@redwood.ai
- Eng SRE on-call: see on-call rota at /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks

Escalation matrix (example):
Issue type -> First point -> Secondary -> Exec escalation
- Access denied for production -> IT Service Desk -> App owner -> CISO
- Incident requiring emergency procurement -> Eng Lead -> VP Finance -> CEO
- Vendor data exposure -> Security -> Legal -> COO

Governance and review cadence:
- This consolidated policy document is reviewed semi-annually by an interlock committee (People Ops, Finance, Security, Eng Platform, Legal).
- Material changes must be announced via All-hands and updated in the Templates library.

Appendix A: Definitions and acronyms
- CAB: Change Advisory Board
- DPA: Data Processing Agreement
- MFA: Multi-factor authentication
- PII: Personally identifiable information
- SLO: Service level objective

Appendix B: Quick links
- Templates library: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates
- Incident Response: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security
- Vendor list & contracts: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process

Revision history:
- 2026-03-04: Initial consolidation (A. Martinez)

If you have questions or need an exception, contact people-ops@redwood.ai and include the policy area and business justification in your message.
